title: From a real need to a live, well-timed session
course_title: Training-of-Trainers (ToT): Teach Adults and Build Trainers

say: From a real need to a live, well-timed session.
This is the video for module two of the Training-of-Trainers course.
Weak trainings start with: what do I want to talk about? Strong ones start with: what must people be able to do afterwards?
Analysis. Talk to five to ten future participants. And ask a hard question: is training the real solution? Training fixes gaps in knowledge and skill, not missing tools or money.

say: For example, Chioma is planning a half-day training for 25 women who sell cooked food at a motor park in Owerri. Her first aim was: participants will understand food hygiene.
But you cannot see someone understand. Words like know or be aware of cannot be observed.

panel.heading: From vague aim to something you can see
right: Explain two ways food is contaminated

say: So she uses Bloom's action verbs. By the end of the session, participants will be able to demonstrate correct hand washing with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds.
Explain two ways uncovered food gets contaminated. And draw up a three-step routine for her own stall.
The formula is: by when, able to, a verb, a task, and a standard.

say: A session plan is the trainer's map: time, activity, what the trainer does, what participants do, and materials. In a ToT, it is your best protection against dilution.
Open with the purpose and objectives in plain words.

items: Experience: role play or case story

Practice, with the trainer moving round

say: Ask open questions starting with what, how or why, and then wait. Count silently to five.
If one woman dominates, thank her, invite someone who has not spoken, and give her a role such as timekeeper.

Use pairs first, and ask her group to report, not her alone.
Write it on a parking lot sheet and return to it at the break.

say: Microteaching is the heart of a ToT. Each trainee teaches a short segment to a small group of peers. For example, in Jos, Rahila teaches a 12-minute segment on filling a savings passbook.

panel.heading: Learn to teach by teaching
items: Teach it to peers for 10 to 15 minutes

say: Feedback is specific and balanced. What went well: your objective was clear. Then situation, behaviour, impact: when you checked the sheets, you corrected errors yourself, so learners did not find out why they were wrong.

panel.heading: Learn to teach by teaching
items: Teach it to peers for 10 to 15 minutes

say: Rahila re-plans and re-teaches the next day, and this time the learners find their own errors.

panel.heading: Learn to teach by teaching
items: Teach it to peers for 10 to 15 minutes

say: The teacher speaks first. Peers give one strength and one improvement each. No one comments on voice, accent or dress.

panel.heading: Learn to teach by teaching
items: Teach it to peers for 10 to 15 minutes
panel.rule: Feedback is about teaching behaviour only, never voice or dress.

say: To remember. Check that training is the real solution. Write objectives with verbs you can see. Every activity supports an objective. Protect settling time, breaks and a buffer. And practise with the microteaching cycle.
